findings.finding: The whole bound rests on three unasserted type-representation assumptions: Variable owns exactly one String (pinned oxrdf 0.3.3), Row = SmallVec<[Id;4]> with Id being POD (no per-row heap other than the spilled buffer, which is rejected), and Vec<Row>/Vec<Variable> buffers being the only other heap. A dependency bump or Id/Row change would silently make the charge an undercount and restore unbounded retention with no test failure.
findings.evidence: capped_rhs_storage charges only rows.capacity()*size_of::<Row>() + vars.capacity()*size_of::<Variable>() + String capacities; supplied oxrdf 0.3.3 source shows `pub struct Variable { name: String }`; report.json accounting notes 'Current pinned oxrdf 0.3.3 Variable owns only String'.
findings.required_action: Add one-line compile-time guards next to the constant, e.g. `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Variable>() == size_of::<String>());` and an equivalent assertion pinning Row's element type/inline width, so representation drift fails the build rather than the invariant.

findings.finding: Soundness of the accounting depends on an unstated coupling: `rhs_cache.get_mut(i).unwrap_or(&mut spare_slot)` may only fall back to the per-step `spare_slot` when `rhs_remaining == 0`. That holds today only because capped_rhs_cache returns either a vec of exactly `len` slots with a positive remainder, or an empty vec with remainder 0. If that pairing were ever broken, a charge would be deducted for an entry that is dropped at end of step and never refunded, monotonically leaking the allowance (silently disabling reuse), not overflowing it.
findings.evidence: capped_rhs_cache returns (Vec::new(), 0) on the disabled/overflow/reserve-failure/capacity-mismatch paths and (slots.len()==len, CAPPED_RHS_STORAGE-bytes) otherwise; capped_rhs unconditionally does `*remaining -= bytes` when storing into whichever slot it was given.
findings.required_action: Add a debug_assert (e.g. `debug_assert!(rhs_cache.len() == prepared.len() || rhs_remaining == 0)`) or make the fallback path explicitly non-charging, plus a one-line comment recording the invariant.

findings.finding: The 4 MiB allowance is per eval_bgp_binary_capped invocation, not per query, per connection or per process. Aggregate retention scales with any concurrent/nested capped evaluations (e.g. per-thread fan-out). Nesting through residual filters appears excluded because EXISTS-bearing shapes are rejected by eligibility, but that is an inherited property, not re-proved by this delta, and the comment does not state the scope.
findings.evidence: capped_rhs_cache/rhs_remaining are locals of eval_bgp_binary_capped; final-*.log 'named EXISTS fallback: [], []' shows zero capped steps for the EXISTS shape; report.json limits paragraph does not mention concurrency scope.
findings.required_action: State the per-invocation scope in the constant's doc comment (and, if the engine can evaluate capped BGPs on multiple threads for one query, note the multiplier) so future readers do not read it as a per-query or per-process cap.

findings.finding: The slot vector is allocated for every eligible capped query even when nothing is ever retained, and for pathological BGPs the slot vector alone can consume the entire allowance with zero reuse benefit (len up to CAPPED_RHS_STORAGE/96 ~= 43,690 patterns is accepted, charging up to ~4 MiB and leaving ~0 remaining).
findings.evidence: two-first case shows +192 B and +1 alloc with no retention (1242 -> 1243 allocs), exactly 2 x size_of::<Option<CappedRhs>> = 2 x 96 B; many-8 minus many-5 peak delta is exactly 288 B = 3 x 96 B, confirming the slot-vector charge model; capped_rhs_cache accepts any len whose slot bytes fit the allowance.
findings.required_action: Optional nit: allocate the slot vector lazily on the first retention attempt, or cap the indexed slot count (e.g. reserve only when len*size is a small fraction of the allowance), so tiny and pathological BGPs pay nothing.

retention_bound_assessment: The bound is real and, unusually, independently corroborated by arithmetic on the measurement data. Every heap object reachable from a retained entry is charged: the slot vector (capacity x size_of::<Option<CappedRhs>>, charged before use and re-checked after try_reserve_exact), rows.capacity() x size_of::<Row>(), vars.capacity() x size_of::<Variable>(), and the String capacity of every live Variable in vars plus sorted_by; inline struct bytes of Bindings/Option<Variable> are already covered by the slot charge. Rows with a spilled SmallVec buffer are rejected rather than estimated, so no uncounted per-row heap can be retained. All products/sums are checked_mul/checked_add with a decline on overflow, try_reserve_exact failure declines reuse, and the post-reserve capacity re-check declines if the allocator over-allocates. Charges are strictly decremented from `remaining` only after a `bytes <= remaining` test, and stale charges are refunded (and the old entry dropped) before the replacement scan, so sum(retained charges) + remaining == CAPPED_RHS_STORAGE is an invariant and total newly-retained heap per invocation is <= 4 MiB. External cross-checks: two-first delta is exactly 192 B = 2 x 96 B slots; many-8 minus many-5 peak delta is exactly 288 B = 3 x 96 B; the many-5 delta minus 480 B of slots is ~2,240,099 B ~= 70,000 x 32 B, i.e. exactly one retained relation, which matches work[2]=10 (2 of 12 scans reused) and 19 (2 of 21), and confirms a second 2.24 MB relation is correctly refused by the remaining ~1.95 MB. Semantics/lifetimes are preserved: reuse is still keyed on (pattern slot, requested sort) with per-pattern-constant filters over an immutable graph; the cached Bindings is only ever handed out as &Bindings to *_ref join kernels; non-fitting scans go to the caller's per-step `uncached` scratch and die at end of step exactly as on main; `slot` and `uncached` are distinct caller locals so the shared 'a lifetime cannot alias; the String move-out/move-back uses only safe consuming API, allocates nothing (String::new()), and restores the Variable before every `?` early return, so no unwind or rejection path can leave a truncated name (asserted by the 'rejected accounting must preserve all capacities' assertion). Armed budgets get an empty slot vector, remaining 0 and hence main's per-step lifetime; the try_capped zk early return is byte-identical. Caveats: the bound covers requested allocation capacities only, not allocator metadata/fragmentation, stack, or any pre-existing AST/planner/NDV/seed/result allocation; it is per eval_bgp_binary_capped invocation; and it silently rests on the pinned oxrdf Variable and Row/Id representations (see findings).
resolved_findings: Unbounded per-pattern RHS retention found by the prior Opus review, Copilot, and the failed many-RHS screen (+11,344,095 B, +104.91%) is genuinely bounded: measured additional peak is now 2,240,579 B / 20.72% (n=5) and 2,240,867 B / 20.72% (n=8), consistent with exactly one retained relation plus the slot vector.

Retention is bound-enforced rather than asserted: the 64 MiB enlarged-allowance control reverts work to [1,3,4,0] and fails the assertion (unbounded.log), i.e. the test would detect removal of the bound.
Capacity-vs-length accounting is mutation-tested: the length mutant reports 58 instead of the executed fixture's 7,360 bytes (length-not-capacity.log).

Stale-charge refund on order replacement is mutation-tested: the no-refund mutant leaves 4,194,247 instead of 4,194,304 and is caught, while the slot is still correctly emptied before the panicking replacement scan (no-refund.log, final-*.log).

Overflow, failed reserve, over-allocating reserve, exact-fit, one-byte-short, oversized row buffer and spilled-Row paths all decline reuse rather than estimate, and are covered by capped_rhs_storage_counts_allocated_capacity / capped_rhs_exact_fit_and_nonfitting_lifetime.

Requested-vs-actual sort distinction survives the rewrite: the cache key remains the requested order while sorted_by stays the scan's truthful value (capped_rhs_keeps_rows_and_actual_order_until_request_changes; changing-sort traces show requested Some(0) with actual Some("s") and reuse only on key match).

performance_claim_limits: No timing claim exists at this head; elapsed-nanos in the counted harness are raw output and must not be read as latency evidence. Extra accounting work (per-candidate O(rows) spilled scan, capacity/String charge loop, slot-vector allocation) is unmeasured.

Memory metrics are requested allocation bytes from a counting allocator: they exclude allocator metadata, fragmentation, transient realloc internals, stack and process-wide effects. RSS and live_after fields include setup/oracle/warmups and must not be equated with query heap.

The +20.72% / ~2.24 MB additional peak and the -2,064,243 B two-miss improvement are specific to these fixtures (70,000 seed rows, all-matching joins, residual-false ASK; 2-pattern first-hit/full-miss), one machine, one allocator, one build profile; they do not generalize to other shapes, datasets or targets, and nothing was measured on wasm32.

The reuse benefit actually realized in the many-RHS fixture is small (2 avoided RHS scans of 12 at n=5, 2 of 21 at n=8), so the memory cost is currently paid for a benefit that has not been quantified in either scans-to-time or end-to-end latency.

Requested metrics were identical across all 3 repetitions, which shows determinism of the counting harness, not statistical evidence about timing or about behaviour under a different allocator/threading configuration.
Test-derived work counts come from debug/test builds with #[cfg(test)] instrumentation and are behavioural, not performance, evidence.
